parser.preparationWhy: Rhino 1.9.2 refuses const in a for…of head and scopes a const to its whole function (a const declared again in a sibling block is a redeclaration error for its parser, not in JavaScript); the reader reads const from the source text

accepted.lowering: imports[alias] = module.name
accepted.where: top level, before functions

accepted.lowering: imports[ns.*] = module
accepted.where: top level, before functions

accepted.construct: const x = e | let x = e | let x
accepted.lowering: local.x = e (undefined without value)
examples:
const total = 0
let count = input.items.length
let found
return { total, count, found }

accepted.construct: const rows = [] | let rows = [], then rows.push(v)
accepted.lowering: json.array({ itemType }) with the type every push proves from its syntax (literals, comparisons, object and list literals)
accepted.where: otherwise FLOWSCRIPT_V3_UNTYPED_LIST with the json.array to write

accepted.lowering: local.a = o.a; local.c = o.b
accepted.limits: one level, no default, no rest
examples:
const { currency, limit: max } = config.billing
return { currency, max }

accepted.construct: x = e | local.x = e | local.o.k = e
examples:
let x = 1
x = 2
local.o = { k: 1 }
local.o.k = 3
result.x = x

accepted.lowering: local.x = local.x + (e); x++ is local.x = Number(local.x) + 1; o.f is a field of a local object or of result, shared as in JavaScript
accepted.where: statement only
examples:
let x = 10
x += 2
x -= 1
x *= 3
x /= 3
x++
x--
return { x }

result.total = input.items.length
result.label = "done"

accepted.lowering: result.a = local.a; result.b = e; return
examples:
const total = input.items.length
return { total, count: total + 1 }

accepted.lowering: return block({ … }): the call writes local.__chain<N>, then return local.__chain<N> (as const row = block({ … }); return row)
examples:
result.n = 1
return
return 3
return text.trim({ text: input.name })

accepted.lowering: a list method or global call the condition always evaluates runs before the if, in a hidden local

accepted.where: no list method in the condition, evaluated before every pass (FLOWSCRIPT_V3_CHAIN)

accepted.lowering: item read as current; an outer item read by a nested loop or arrow is copied to local.item; items may be Object.keys(o), Object.values(o) or a chain, computed once before the loop

accepted.construct: for (let i = a; i < b; i++) {…}
accepted.limits: < or <=, step ++, i not assigned in the body; maxIterations 1000000
accepted.lowering: local.i = a; while (i < b) { body; local.i = Number(local.i) + 1 }

accepted.construct: for (let i = a; i < b; i++) { … continue … }
accepted.where: i not assigned in the body
accepted.lowering: a hidden counter local.__count<N> steps before the body, continue is next, the bound is read at every test

accepted.limits: literal labels, every case ends with break/return/throw, default last
examples:
switch (input.items.length) {
  case 2:
    result.value = "two"
    break
  case 3:
    result.value = "three"
    break
  default:
    result.value = "other"
    break
}

accepted.lowering: error = local.e, read as e inside the catch only, e.details the details of the thrown error (undefined without); catch {…} declares no name: local.error, or a hidden local.__caught<N> when the Flow has its own error

accepted.where: while, for…of or counted for, no label

examples: throw { code: "NAME_REQUIRED", message: "name is required", status: 400 }

accepted.where: e is the parameter of an enclosing catch (a const)
accepted.lowering: throw({ error: "local.e" }): the caught error again, unchanged (application or failure)
same as a.b (paths are null-safe)
examples: return { count: input?.items?.length, first: input?.items?.[0] }

const active = input.rows.filter(row => row.active)
return { active }

const first = input.rows.find(row => row.vip)
return { first }

const anyLate = input.rows.some(row => row.late)
return { anyLate }

const allPaid = input.rows.every(row => row.paid)
return { allPaid }

accepted.construct: xs.toSorted((a, b) => a.k - b.k) | xs.toSorted((a, b) => a - b) | xs.toSorted((a, b) => a.k.localeCompare(b.k)) | xs.toSorted((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b)) | [...xs].sort((a, b) => b.k - a.k)

properties.by: current.k for a key comparator; omitted for an identity comparator (the block uses current)

accepted.note: a copy sorted by Array.prototype.sort with the arrow's comparator; without compare, the Flow order
examples:
const copy = [...input.rows].sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)
return { copy }

accepted.construct: xs.toSorted((a, b) => a.k < b.k ? -1 : (a.k > b.k ? 1 : 0)), and every ternary of comparisons of the two keys with the same sign for every pair

properties.compare: natural: a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0 on the raw keys

accepted.note: checked on the eight classes of a key pair; a.k < b.k ? -1 : 1 is refused

accepted.construct: xs.toSorted((a, b) => c1 || c2 || …), each ci a key comparator

properties.then: [{ by, compare, direction }, …] for c2, c3…

accepted.note: c1 || c2 evaluated literally: a 0 or NaN falls to the next key

accepted.lowering: one node per block step, linked by local.__chain<N>
accepted.where: assignment, return, if condition; not in && || ?? branches, a ?: inside an expression, a call argument, after a scope read, a while condition

accepted.lowering: if (cond) { x = branch1 } else { x = branch2 }, each chain lowered in its branch
accepted.where: a declaration, assignment or returned field that is entirely the ?:

accepted.lowering: the expression method Array.prototype.concat; a chain in an argument runs before it

accepted.where: rows created by json.array, or by const rows = [] / let rows = [] whose item type every push proves
byId created by json.map or declared with an object literal (const groups = {}); a finite number key is its text, as in JavaScript; any other computed key is FLOWSCRIPT_V3_COMPUTED_WRITE
assignment, return, chain head, if condition, for…of list
examples:
const keys = Object.keys({ a: 1, b: 2 })
return { keys }

accepted.where: assignment, return, chain head, if condition, for…of list
examples:
const values = Object.values({ a: 1, b: 2 })
return { values }

accepted.where: assignment, return, chain head, if condition
examples:
const value = JSON.parse("{\"a\":1}")
return { value }

accepted.where: assignment, return, chain head, if condition

accepted.construct: /p/f.test(s) | s.match(/p/f) | s.replace(/p/f, y) | s.replaceAll(/p/g, y) | s.split(/p/f)
accepted.lowering: the block in local.__chain<N> before the statement: text.match({ text: String(s), pattern: "p", flags }) read as .matched (test) or .matched ? .groups : null (match); text.replace and text.split with regex: true
accepted.where: whole value of a declaration, an assignment or a return, a branch of a whole ?:, a place a value or an if condition always evaluates, the list of a for…of (split, match); flags among g, i, m and s; elsewhere FLOWSCRIPT_V3_PATTERN

accepted.lowering: the call writes local.__chain<N> before the statement, then the expression reads local.__chain<N>.field (as const r = block({ … }); const field = r.field)
accepted.where: whole value of a declaration, an assignment or a return, a branch of a whole ?:, a place a value or an if condition always evaluates; elsewhere FLOWSCRIPT_V3_CALL_RESULT
examples:
const second = text.split({ text: input.csv, separator: "," })[1]
return { second, upper: text.trim({ text: input.name }).toUpperCase() }

accepted.lowering: expression function default (null, undefined and "" replaced)
accepted.where: any expression; a bare default( is refused (FLOWSCRIPT_V3_RESERVED_WORD)
properties beyond the JavaScript form; a slot is $$s() {…}, $$s: function () {…} or $$s: () => {…}; assigned or returned, the call writes $$out

accepted.lowering: explicit node name

accepted.construct: // text or /* text */ above a statement, no blank line
accepted.lowering: node comment (formatter writes // lines); standalone comment node after a blank line
$$disabled: true

accepted.construct: function helper({ a, b }) { … } after the Flow function, called helper({ a: 1 })
accepted.lowering: helper block, as in v2; body under the same rules

refused.construct: import … from "…"
declaring or importing flow, a scope name, or a local starting with __
default(x, y) outside a switch: default is a reserved word, so this is not JavaScript
refused.rewrite: flow.default(x, y), with the same arguments

refused.construct: a local named like a block namespace the Flow uses (text, list, json…)
x and local.x in the same Flow
a name read outside the block that declares it
refused.rewrite: declare it in the enclosing block

refused.construct: a name declared again in an enclosed block, or hiding an import or a loop variable
assigning a const
destructuring with default, rest or nesting
x++ or x += e inside an expression
result.x = … and return { … } in the same Flow
break
refused.rewrite: a local tested by the while condition, or find / filter

refused.construct: finally
return inside a loop
refused.rewrite: continue, or a local and a return after the loop

refused.construct: a for (;;) other than for (let i = a; i < b; i++), or a counter assigned in the body
refused.rewrite: for…of, or a while with a local the body changes

refused.construct: switch with fall-through, non-literal case or default not last
refused.example:
switch (input.items.length) {
  case 1:
    result.x = 1
  case 2:
    result.x = 2
    break
}

refused.construct: do … while, for … in, labelled loop, labelled break or continue
a function other than a top-level helper, a list arrow or a slot (nested, in an expression, a closure); a slot with a parameter or an expression body
refused.rewrite: inline, a top-level helper, or a project block; a slot $$s() {…}

refused.construct: a block method in && || ?? branches, a ?: inside an expression or its test, a call argument, after a scope read, a while condition
xs.sort alone, an inexact comparator (a.k < b.k ? -1 : 1…), reduce, (x, i), an outer arrow parameter in an inner arrow
refused.rewrite: toSorted with a.k - b.k, localeCompare or a.k < b.k ? -1 : a.k > b.k ? 1 : 0, joined by ||; list.sum, list.map or a loop
refused.example: const total = input.rows.reduce((sum, row) => sum + row.amount, 0)

refused.construct: const rows = [] then a push of no certain type, or of different types
refused.rewrite: json.array({ itemType }) with the type of the pushed values

refused.construct: Object.* or JSON.* elsewhere or with other arguments, Object.entries, Date.now, new Date
throw new Error(m)
async, await, generators, classes, this, new, const without a value, o.f++ on a loop item or input, throw of a name that is not a catch parameter, a thrown object with an error field
if or while whose condition is an object literal
a regular expression literal in a lazy place (after && || ??, in a list arrow, an argument, a while condition) or in another form
refused.rewrite: const m = text.match({ text: String(s), pattern: "p" }) before the statement, then m.matched

refused.construct: a field of a block call result read in a lazy place (after && || ??, a branch of a ?: inside an expression, an argument, a list arrow, a while condition, a for…of list)
refused.rewrite: const r = block({ … }) in its own statement, then r.field
refused.example: const size = input.name != "" && text.trim({ text: input.name }).length

refused.construct: a write under a computed key elsewhere than on a local object or map (result[k], a loop item, a list item, a nested field, an input), groups[k].push(v)
refused.rewrite: const groups = {} then groups[k] = v, and result.groups = groups; groups[k] = groups[k].concat([v])

valueRules: paths are null-safe (undefined instead of a TypeError)
<, <=, >, >= compare two numeric texts as numbers
a template literal writes null and undefined as "", objects and lists as JSON
loops have an execution budget: while 1000 passes and 60 s unless flow.while sets other bounds; counted for 1000000 passes

rendering.default: natural JavaScript form wherever the meaning is identical, call form otherwise; author forms kept through __flowScript* node fields

names.loopVariable: item, then item2, item3… when visible

conformance.why: Rhino 1.9.2 keeps the first value of a const declared in a block nested in a loop (#326); v3 lowers each declaration to an assignment at every pass
conformance.rule: run by the Flow engine from the lowered tree, never by evaluating the text with Rhino; no const is rewritten

conformance.why: flow.default is the v2 default function written as JavaScript: undefined, null and "" give the fallback, in any expression; a bare default( is a reserved word, not a call
conformance.rule: the source is read by the Rhino 1.9.2 parser (ES6) as written, without preparation or error; run by the Flow engine from the lowered tree

conformance.why: Rhino 1.9.2 scopes a const to its whole function: a const declared again in a sibling block or a later for…of is a redeclaration for its parser, while JavaScript scopes each one to its block (the L3 bench refusal of 18/11)
conformance.rule: parsed after the same-length preparation that writes each const declaration keyword as let; each declaration keeps its const rule
